new_findings.location: 7.1 release row ('This row assumes Iroh in V1 ... so 4/4'); 7.3 bullets 1-2 ('Rust's lead is 0.40'; 'Go 3.70, Rust 3.65, a tie'); 9 ('if Iroh is deferred the comparison is a tie'); 10 Q-A ('Deferral makes the comparison a tie').
new_findings.claim: With Iroh in V1 Rust leads by 0.40; with Iroh deferred the comparison is a tie.
new_findings.evidence: Each anchor uses the re-scorer reading most favourable to Go, and neither range is shown. In V1: rescore-r4/fable/scores.md line 128 ('If Iroh is in V1, Go 3 / Rust 4') and opus/scores.json release basis ('With Iroh: Go 3, Rust 4. The 4/4 is the probability-weighted midpoint') read the row as 3/4; only Codex scores 4/4 with Iroh ('setting release 4/4', codex/scores.md line 155); the round-1 draft of this revision also said 'in V1 about Go 3 / Rust 4'; orchestrator-prereg.md describes its 4/4 as 'Offsetting; Go leads without Iroh, Rust with it', i.e. a cross-scenario judgment, not a V1 one. Under 3/4 the totals are Go 3.30 / Rust 3.90, a 0.60 lead. Deferred: Codex (demonstrated path) and Fable read the row as Go 4 / Rust 3; only Opus gives Go 5 / Rust 3, the value 7.3 adopts. Under Go 4 / Rust 3 with ecosystem 4/3 the deferred totals are Go 3.50 / Rust 3.65 (Rust by 0.15); with cross-platform also 4/4, Go 3.75 / Rust 3.65. The direction is unchanged and the selection is conservative against the recommendation, but the owner is told the largest lever produces '0.40 to a tie' when the four scorings' readings span '0.40-0.60 to between Rust +0.15 and Go +0.05'. The change of the orchestrator's own V1 judgment from 3/4 (draft) to 4/4 (now) is not explained anywhere.
new_findings.fix: In 7.3, add the ranges: 'Release row Go 3 / Rust 4 in V1 (two re-scorers and the draft of this revision): Go 3.30, Rust 3.90, a 0.60 lead' and 'Deferred with release Go 4 / Rust 3 (two re-scorers): Go 3.50, Rust 3.65; with Go 5 / Rust 3: 3.70 / 3.65'. Reword Q-A and 9: 'Deferral narrows the lead to between a 0.15 Rust lead and a 0.05 Go lead, a tie within the precision of these judgments.' In the 7.1 release row, say the 4/4 V1 reading is the Codex reading and that the two Claude re-scorers read V1 as 3/4.

new_findings.location: 10 D3 (l), last sentence: 'The rubric was set by the orchestrator after the per-cell reviews disagreed, and applied by agents that did not know which cell's reviewer had rated what.'
new_findings.claim: The calibrated rubric was applied blind to the per-cell reviewers' ratings.
new_findings.evidence: tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x2/t1-calibration/README.md: the uniform classification is 'one row per (cell, defect): every defect the cell's reviewer listed (D1 = first defect in results.json ...)', each table has a 'reviewer' column holding the cell reviewer's severity next to the calibrated 'class', and a section 'Where this contradicts a reviewer' lists 'go-opus2 D1 (reviewer minor -> major)', 'rust-sonnet1 D1 (reviewer major -> minor)'. The 'Independent check' was 'given the same rubric, results.json, the scripts, matrix.md, extra.md and raw/, but not this classification', and results.json carries the cell reviews (x2/RESULTS.md section 8: 'per cell, the implementer report, evaluation, review and usage'). cross-review/T3/README.md likewise 'confirms or refutes each reviewer-listed defect'. So both classifiers knew the reviewers' ratings; what the second was blind to is the first classification. The sentence is in the ruling text the owner is asked to ratify and overstates the independence of the pro-Rust T1 count on exactly the provenance point M3 raised. (My round-1 'blind re-classification' was the imprecise source; the record supports 'blind to the first classification'.)
new_findings.fix: Replace with: 'applied by one agent per task that re-rated every defect the cell reviewers had listed, with the reviewers' ratings in view; for T1 a second agent, given the same evidence but not the first classification, reached the same three majors and no Rust major.'

new_findings.location: 10 D3 (k) and contract 9.7: 'Exploiting the path needs control of both a directory name on it and an environment variable.'
new_findings.claim: Both prerequisites are needed to exploit the batch-path expansion.
new_findings.evidence: x1b-review-rust.json defects[0]: (a) the injected command needed an attacker-controlled variable plus a directory named pct%HMRDIRVAR%x; (b) 'os%OS%y\fwd.bat ran a different batch file' using the standard %OS% variable, so wrong-file execution needs only a %-bearing path and an existing directory. The threat-model conclusion survives (whoever controls the path can already name any file), but the sentence states the prerequisites for the injection case only.
new_findings.fix: 'Command injection through the path needs an attacker-controlled environment variable and a matching directory; wrong-file execution needs only a % in the path and a directory, which control of the path already gives.'

new_findings.location: 9, Go paragraph: 'All are fixable or avoidable, as one implementer in each X2 task showed.'

No Go T1 cell avoided the major; 6.2 correctly says 'one Go cell partly avoided the trap'. The T1 fixes are named by the verification, not shown by an implementer.
new_findings.fix: 'All are fixable (the T1 verification names standard-library fixes) or avoidable (one T3 implementer repainted around wide text).'

section_10_answerable: Yes, in one sitting. D1 is a three-way choice; Q-A to Q-F are yes/no or either/or, each with its consequence stated; D3 (a)-(l) default to 'stand', so the owner only flags exceptions. Two improvements, neither blocking: order the questions by dependency rather than effect (Q-D and Q-C first: may D1 be recorded now; then Q-A: which scenario; then D3 (k), (l), Q-E, Q-F: which readings; then D1), and add one line stating the default path ('answering every default, Iroh in V1, rulings stand, decide now, gives Rust by 0.40 with low confidence; the ranges in 7.3 bound it'). After N1, Q-A's consequence should read 'narrows to a tie within precision' rather than 'makes it a tie'.
same_recommendation_and_confidence: Yes. Rust + Ratatui, low confidence, conditional on Iroh staying in V1. With Iroh in V1 every scoring and every V1 reading of the release row (4/4 or 3/4) leaves Rust ahead by 0.40-0.60; with Iroh deferred the readings span Rust +0.15 to Go +0.05, which is a tie within the precision these judgments have. The two new majors do not move the direction: N1 widens the shown range (in Rust's favour under V1, toward Rust under deferral), and N2 corrects an independence claim about the T1 count without changing the count. Confidence stays low for the round-1 reasons, now disclosed in the ADR: the four scorings share one X2 reading, the T1 half of the maintainability signal is an inherited architecture effect, and the 3-0 split exists in one of three rubric readings.
summary: Of the 15 round-1 findings, 11 are resolved and 4 partly (M3: the added mitigation clause overclaims; m2: no path for the Codex model; m5 and m8: 7.1 or 9 still carry one side of a pair). No finding is unresolved in substance, and the fidelity fixes introduced no new asymmetry except a one-sided unsafe count (N3). Two new majors, both one-paragraph fixes and neither changing the direction: N1, the sensitivity anchors (0.40 lead; deferral is a tie) each adopt the re-scorer reading most favourable to Go without showing the range (V1 read as 3/4 by two re-scorers and the draft gives 0.60; deferral read as Go 4 / Rust 3 by two re-scorers leaves Rust 0.15 ahead), and the orchestrator's own V1 judgment moved from 3/4 to 4/4 unexplained; N2, D3 (l) says the rubric was applied by agents who did not know the cell reviewers' ratings, while the calibration record re-rates every reviewer-listed defect with the reviewer's rating in a column and the independent check was blind only to the first classification. Seven minors: Go's 30 unsafe sites omitted next to Rust's 20; the security-core row citing 6.2 while disclaiming X2; 'low to medium' in the 7.2 table against 'low' in 9; the D3 (k) attacker prerequisites stated for the injection case only; 'avoidable, as one implementer in each X2 task showed' false for T1; T1-alone committed to 3/4 while T3-alone is left open; an X4 citation that should be X1b. Section 10 is answerable in one sitting. Same recommendation and confidence as round 1.
